sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Endowment Management for Philanthropic and Scientific Grants

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Unitary National Legal System; not a common-law or Sharia jurisdiction; centrally unified company and AML/CFT law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Bilateral Investment Treaty between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Ultimate Beneficial Owner's Home Jurisdiction (specific treaty to be identified by UNCTAD and PRC Ministry of Commerce after UBO confirmation)

Convention between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Ultimate Beneficial Owner's Home Jurisdiction for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income (specific DTAA to be identified after UBO confirmation)
Agreement on Investment among the Governments of the People's Republic of China, Japan and the Republic of Korea (applicable only to Japanese or Korean UBOs)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: PBOC/SAMR Administrative Measures for Beneficial Owner Information of Market Entities (Order No. 3 [2024], effective 1 November 2024); PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law (2024 Revision, effective 1 January 2025); Company Law of the PRC (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024); Foreign Investment Law of the PRC (effective 1 January 2020); Special Administrative Measures (Negative List) for Foreign Investment Access (2024); Regulations on the Administration of Foundations (State Council, 2004); Charity Law of the PRC (2016)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the UBO/shareholder's home jurisdiction (for example, Companies House, ACRA or a similar Registrar)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the issuing state is an HCCH Apostille Convention member: notarized/certified copy -> Apostille issued by the designated Competent Authority -> certified Simplified Chinese translation; no Chinese consular legalization. If the issuing state is a non-member: notarized copy -> authentication by the originating state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs/State Department -> Chinese Embassy or Consulate legalization -> certified Simplified Chinese translation; no Apostille. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel, never chainable.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Active Status
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the foreign shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the issuing state is an Apostille member: official certificate -> Apostille -> certified Chinese translation; no consular legalization. If a non-member: official certificate -> authentication by originating state MFA/State Department -> Chinese Embassy/Consulate legalization -> certified Chinese translation; no Apostille. Use either path depending solely on membership status.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing formation of the WFOE
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or equivalent governing body of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature page -> Apostille if home state is an Apostille member; otherwise MFA authentication and Chinese Embassy/Consulate legalization; then certified Chinese translation. Never add Apostille to a consular-legalized document or vice versa.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum of Association / Constitutional Documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign shareholder's corporate registry or registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy -> Notarization -> Apostille for Apostille-convention states, or notarization -> MFA authentication -> Chinese Embassy/Consulate legalization for non-member states; then certified Chinese translation. The two authentication routes are mutually exclusive.

Original bank letter on bank letterhead with authorized signature -> signature notarization -> Apostille if the bank's jurisdiction is an Apostille member; otherwise notarization -> MFA authentication -> Chinese Embassy/Consulate legalization; then certified Chinese translation if the bank is not a PRC bank.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before filing, all UBOs, directors, managers, authorized signatories, banks and major counterparties must be screened against UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, Chinese unreliable-entity and export-control lists, OFAC SDN and non-SDN restrictions, EU/UK sanctions where relevant, domestic and foreign PEP databases, and adverse media. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for PEPs and transactions connected with high-risk jurisdictions. Any name, passport, address or control-link match requires beneficial-ownership recalculation, source-of-wealth evidence, independent risk approval, and suspicious-transaction reporting to the competent anti-money-laundering authority before incorporation closes.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Registration System and National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) operated by SAMR and provincial Administrations for Market Regulation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name must follow the statutory four-tier Chinese naming formula: administrative division + distinctive Chinese trade name + industry description + organizational form. The name must be in Simplified Chinese; a foreign investor may adopt a Chinese trade name that is a phonetic transliteration of its corporate name, but may not register an English-only name. For this scope, if the vehicle is truly a private charitable foundation, PRC law requires the organizational form 'Foundation' (as a special non-profit legal person approved by the Ministry of Civil Affairs), whereas a WFOE must use 'Limited Liability Company' as its organizational form; the word 'Foundation' in a WFOE name is prohibited unless the entity is converted to a licensed foundation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Following an automatic rejection decision, the applicant may within 60 calendar days of receipt file administrative reconsideration before the superior Administration for Market Regulation or the same-level people's government, and may later appeal to the people's court within six months of the reconsideration result. If the rejection was based on a correctable defect, refiling with a revised Chinese trade name is quicker. A pre-approved name may be extended once for another 30 days before expiry by applying through the SAMR portal; after expiry the reservation lapses and a new application is required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the sole registered address for a WFOE engaged in endowment management, philanthropic grant-making, or fund management. PRC company registration and tax administration practice require a fixed, leased or owned physical business premises. The tax authority applies the place-of-effective-management test and may disregard a shell address; PBOC-regulated banks conducting on-site verification will refuse corporate account opening when the only address is a virtual office. This industry requires physical presence evidenced by office lease invoices, utility bills, staff payroll and social-insurance records.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (i) executed lease for at least one year; (ii) rent and property-management invoices; (iii) corporate nameplate at the registered address; (iv) staff present with labor contracts and social-insurance records; (v) statutory books, board minutes, UBO filings and grant/end

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 23-33, 47, 59-75; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2020), Articles 4, 16-18, 26; Charity Law of the People's Republic of China (2016, amended 2023); Regulations on the Administration of Registration of Social Organizations and Foundations, as applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) / local Market Supervision and Administration Bureau (MSA) at the proposed registered office jurisdiction, through the foreign-investment one-stop registration window and the National Enterprise Registration Online Service.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration and Articles of Association filed through the National Enterprise Registration Online Service; the business license issued under the Unified Social Credit Code system.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None (no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a WFOE limited liability company under the 2023 Company Law). Under Article 47, all subscribed capital must be fully paid within five years from incorporation unless the Articles of Association require an earlier contribution schedule. No blocked escrow account is required by company law; however, if the entity is registered as a charitable foundation, the civil affairs authority may require proof of an endowment account and grant-funding commitments.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] (WHOLLY FOREIGN-OWNED LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY). The undersigned, constituting the full Board of Directors of [COMPANY NAME] (the Company), acting by unanimous written consent in lieu of a meeting, adopt the following resolutions and hereby mandate the actions described below. WHEREAS the Company is to be incorporated under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China as a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company for the purpose of endowment management for philanthropic and scientific grants; and WHEREAS the sole shareholder has subscribed to the registered capital set out in the Articles of Association; and WHEREAS the Articles of Association empower the Board to adopt all incidental resolutions necessary for incorporation and initial administration; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The registered capital of the Company shall be [AMOUNT] in the currency stated in the Articles of Association. The sole shareholder shall subscribe to the entire registered capital and shall pay the subscribed capital in accordance with the contribution schedule in the Articles of Association, provided that all capital contributions shall be fully paid no later than five years from the date of issuance of the business license, or by such earlier date as the Articles prescribe. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board authorizes the opening of bank accounts at [BANK NAME], including the basic deposit account, a foreign currency capital account if needed, and an endowment/grant distribution account. The legal representative and the finance manager shall be designated as joint signatories. All grant distributions, endowment investments, and bank wires shall require dual authorization under the Company's expenditure control policy, and no single officer shall have unilateral release authority. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The registered office of the Company is fixed at [ADDRESS]. The legal representative is authorized to execute and deliver the lease agreement, to obtain the domicile certificate, and to file all registered-office proofs with the local Market Supervision and Administration Bureau. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: [NAME] is appointed Director and Chairperson; [NAME] is appointed Legal Representative; [NAME] is appointed General Manager; and [NAME] is appointed Supervisor. Each appointed officer shall serve until the first annual shareholders' meeting or until earlier removal or resignation. The Supervisor shall not concurrently hold the office of Legal Representative, General Manager, or Finance Manager. 5. FILING AND INCIDENTAL AUTHORITY: The Chairperson and Legal Representative, acting jointly, are authorized to execute all registration applications, articles, declarations, bank forms, and regulatory filings, and to engage a licensed PRC law firm and certified agents to effect the business license, tax registration, civil affairs filing, and all ancillary permits. RESOLVED FURTHER that this resolution shall be filed in the corporate minute book and a certified copy delivered to each statutory officer and the registered bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Reservation, Negative List Screening, and Business Scope Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration Online Service / local Market Supervision and Administration Bureau (MSA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an enterprise name reservation through the MSA online portal or the SAMR National Enterprise Registration Online Service. The applicant must select the limited liability company form, provide the proposed English name and Chinese transliteration, define the business scope as endowment management for philanthropic and scientific grants, and self-certify that the proposed operations are outside the Foreign Investment Negative List. The application must identify the proposed directors, supervisor, and legal representative, and include the foreign shareholder's basic identification data. If the name reservation is approved, the name is reserved for a period of two months, and the subsequent registration application must be submitted before the reservation expires.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name in English and Chinese transliteration
Passport or certified copy of the sole foreign shareholder
Identification data of proposed directors, supervisor, and legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected, submit up to three alternative names and correct the business scope wording. If the negative-list self-assessment is queried, obtain a written PRC legal opinion confirming permissibility under the Foreign Investment Law and resubmit the application with the opinion attached.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Notarization, and Apostille of Constitutional and Corporate Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: PRC notary office; foreign notary and competent authority of the shareholder's jurisdiction under the Hague Apostille Convention
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a PRC-licensed law firm or authorized agent to prepare the Articles of Association, shareholder resolution, first director and supervisor appointment instruments, legal representative appointment letter, capital contribution schedule, and registered-office lease. The foreign shareholder's certificate of incorporation or passport, corporate resolutions, powers of attorney, and beneficial ownership statement must be notarized in the jurisdiction of origin and apostilled in accordance with the Hague Apostille Convention, which applies to China. All documents not originally in English must be translated into English by a certified translator. The legal representative's identification and residential address must be verified against the translated documents before electronic filing.
required_dossiers: Apostilled certificate of incorporation or passport of the foreign shareholder
Certified English translations of all foreign-language documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the apostille or notarization is rejected or deficient, cure by obtaining a corrected translation, renewing the apostille, or completing a legalization chain through the competent authority. If the shareholder entity cannot provide current corporate records, provide successor legal capacity evidence and a fresh certificate of good standing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Online Submission of Company Registration Application to the Local MSA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision and Administration Bureau (MSA), Foreign Investment One-Stop Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the company registration application through the local MSA foreign-investment one-stop window by uploading the approved name reservation, Articles of Association, apostilled and notarized shareholder documents, domicile certificate, lease, capital contribution schedule, and identification copies of the directors, supervisor, and legal representative. The legal representative must complete an electronic signature through the official identity verification application or using a digital certificate. The MSA reviews the application for compliance with the Company Law, the Foreign Investment Law, and the entity's proposed business scope. Upon approval, the MSA issues the business license with a Unified Social Credit Code. The registry may issue a correction letter or request supplemental documents before final approval.
required_dossiers: Apostilled or notarized foreign shareholder documents
Identification copies of directors, supervisor, and legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MSA issues a query or correction notice, respond within 15 days with the requested supplemental documents. If registration is suspended because of an impermissible business scope, amend the Articles to exclude restricted activities or request administrative reconsideration before the local MSA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Foreign Direct Investment Registration with SAFE
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through the bank's direct FDI registration system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the basic deposit account, and if needed, a foreign currency capital account at a licensed commercial bank. The bank will perform KYC/AML due diligence and request the business license, Articles of Association, board resolution on bank accounts, company seal, finance seal, legal representative identification, and proof of registered office. The bank will submit the foreign direct investment information registration to SAFE through the direct bank application system. The foreign shareholder's capital contribution must be remitted with the remittance purpose code for registered capital, converted in accordance with SAFE rules, and credited to the capital account. The bank will issue a capital contribution receipt, which must be archived in the corporate minute book and used for grant distribution and endowment management compliance.
required_dossiers: Company seal, finance seal, and legal representative seal
FDI registration form prepared by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account opening for KYC reasons, provide additional beneficial ownership documentation, source-of-funds evidence, and a board resolution clarifying signatories. If SAFE registration fails, correct the remittance purpose code with the remitting bank and resubmit the FDI information through the receiving bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Charitable Foundation Civil Affairs Filing and Tax-Exempt Status Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Civil Affairs / local civil affairs authority in the registered-office jurisdiction; local tax authority for non-profit status
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the business scope is classified under ISIC 6430 and NAICS 813211 as an endowment-management and private charitable foundation vehicle, the company must complete the applicable civil affairs registration or charity organization designation. Prepare and file the foundation charter, grant-making policy, endowment funds plan, and statutory officers' sworn undertaking to comply with the Charity Law of the People's Republic of China. If the entity only administers grants as a commercial WFOE and does not publicly hold itself out as a charitable foundation, this civil affairs step is replaced by such financial or investment advisory licensing as may apply. After civil affairs approval, apply to the tax authority for non-profit status if the endowment income is intended to be tax-exempt, and thereafter comply with annual inspection, public fundraising reporting, and grant-distribution transparency requirements.
required_dossiers: Board resolution authorizing civil affairs filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the civil affairs authority rejects the foundation registration, revise the foundation charter, remove public fundraising features, and reapply. If the rejection is based on legal capacity or structure, obtain counsel to convert the vehicle into a non-foundation grant-management limited company or request administrative reconsideration before the civil affairs authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. The entity is classified under ISIC 6430 / NAICS 813211 and does not operate a manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facility.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable as an industrial operating license. The statutory authorization required for the charitable endowment scope is the charitable foundation registration or charity organization designation issued by the civil affairs authority.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable; Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China would be the competent agency only if a physical project were separately constructed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable / Exempt under the List of Fixed Asset Investment Projects Subject to Environmental Impact Assessment (2021 Edition), because no construction, production, or waste-generating facility is created.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. No industrial wastewater, volatile organic compound emissions, or hazardous waste are generated. The registered office generates only municipal domestic sewage and ordinary office solid waste, both discharged through municipal systems in compliance with local utility standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable. No Civil Defense fire permit, structural-load inspection, or workplace-safety certification is required because the entity has no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing premises. The office lease must nonetheless include the landlord's fire-safety certificate and ensure general egress, fire-extinguisher readiness, and basic occupational health compliance for administrative workers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; online filings are processed through the National Electronic Tax Administration (e-Tax / Electronic Tax Bureau) platform at the STA branch covering the WFOE's registered address.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Incorporate the foreign-invested WFOE under the Foreign Investment Law of the PRC and the PRC Company Law; if licensed as a charitable endowment entity, first obtain the statutory charitable foundation license from the competent civil affairs authority. Step 2 - Register with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and receive the Business License containing the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC); the USCC is automatically the taxpayer identification number (TIN) for all national taxes, including VAT. Step 3 - Complete integrated tax registration via the STA e-Tax platform or through SAMR/STA data sharing by filing legal representative details, financial institution account information, accounting software/policy, and tax practitioner contact. No separate VAT certificate or TIN is issued because the USCC serves both enterprise income tax and VAT identification. For a foreign non-resident entity without a PRC establishment, tax obligations are generally satisfied by withholding at source; if the non-resident itself creates a taxable presence through a fixed place, service establishment, or digital supply platform in China, it must complete tax registration with the competent STA office and obtain an STA-assigned taxpayer identification number through the e-Tax system. Step 4 - If recognized as a charitable/non-profit foundation, apply for the state tax-exemption qualification with the fiscal and tax authorities and file the charitable status certificate with the STA. Step 5 - Determine VAT taxpayer status: below RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable turnover the WFOE is a small-scale VAT taxpayer; upon exceeding the threshold it must be classified as a general VAT taxpayer, which is also required to export goods under zero-rating and claim input VAT refunds.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for US-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections; the PRC applies entity-level taxation to WFOEs. VAT status elections are administrative: a small-scale VAT taxpayer may voluntarily apply for general VAT taxpayer status below the RMB 5,000,000 threshold, and mandatory general status applies above it. Charitable tax exemption is not an elective classification but requires an approved non-profit qualification application.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable sales (turnover) is the mandatory transition threshold for general VAT taxpayer status; all licensed enterprises are automatically registered for VAT from incorporation with no minimum monetary threshold. Overseas remote sellers providing taxable digital services or goods to PRC consumers may have VAT registration or collection obligations when their economic nexus meets the conditions under the E-Commerce Law and cross-border VAT rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates VAT invoice issuance exclusively through STA-controlled tax control and e-invoice systems. The fully digitalized e-invoice reform requires issuance, transmission, acceptance, and red-letter reversal through the National Electronic Tax Administration e-invoice service platform, with real-time reporting to the STA and a unique anti-fraud digital stamp or QR code on each invoice. Large taxpayers integrate their ERP systems with the e-invoice platform using certified APIs or third-party e-invoice service providers; invoice allocation, data integrity, and reconciliation are supervised under Golden Tax Phase IV, and any mismatch between invoice data and VAT returns can suspend invoice quotas or trigger penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods, 0% export VAT applies when the WFOE is a general VAT taxpayer, the goods are physically exported from China and cleared by Customs, title and risk are transferred to an overseas purchaser, the export sales price is supported by contract and invoices, and the proceeds are paid in foreign currency and repatriated to China within the foreign-exchange collection period. For cross-border services, including qualifying offshore endowment or fund management services, zero-rating is available only when the service recipient is located outside China, the service is performed wholly outside China, the contract and invoice are properly executed, and foreign-currency remittance proves the offshore commercial nature. Domestic charitable grant distribution or domestic fund administration does not qualify for export zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) for the exported goods, with commodity code, quantity, value, destination and exporter details matching the VAT refund claim
Bill of Lading, sea waybill, air waybill or other internationally recognized transport document proving physical export from China
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or equivalent bank-generated proof of foreign-currency repatriation from the overseas buyer into the exporter's PRC bank account
Export sales contract and commercial invoice signed with the overseas customer
Customs inspection/quarantine certificate or product compliance certificate where the exported goods are subject to statutory inspection
Special VAT invoice or export invoice data transmitted to the STA electronic tax control and export refund platform
Any additional packing list, insurance certificate, or freight evidence required by China Customs or STA to verify the export transaction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export VAT refunds are audited through cross-matching of Customs export declarations, e-invoice data, logistics records, and SAFE foreign-exchange receipt data. If zero-rating is claimed without actual export, without valid foreign-currency receipt, after the 180-day repatriation deadline, or with forged documents, the refund is clawed back with interest, the export transaction is recharacterized as taxable supply, and penalties are assessed under the Law of the People's Republic of China on Tax Administration and Tax Collection at 50% to 5 times the defrauded refund amount. Criminal exposure for fraudulent export tax refund under Article 204 of the PRC Criminal Law includes imprisonment up to life, fines, and confiscation of property; responsible officers and the WFOE may also face collection enforcement, loss of export refund eligibility, and cancellation of charitable tax-exempt status.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) in conjunction with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a managed floating exchange rate regime with limited capital account convertibility. The RMB is freely convertible for current account transactions, including trade in goods and services, dividends, and interest, provided that genuine underlying business documentation is presented. Capital account transactions require prior approval or registration with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE). A wholly foreign-owned enterprise must complete foreign investment registration under the FDI system; each inbound capital injection is reported via the SAFE capital registration platform and reconciled at the domestic bank through a Foreign Exchange Capital Account. Funds credited as registered paid-in capital may be converted into RMB upon submission of a capital verification report prepared by a licensed PRC accounting firm, and the RMB proceeds must comply with the negative list and business scope. Profit remittance to offshore shareholders is classified as a current-account item after corporate income tax settlement, but the remittance bank will require audited financial statements, tax payment certificates, and a shareholders resolution approving the dividend. For a private charitable foundation, cross-border donations and grants are subject to the Overseas Donations Regulation and the PRC Charity Law, and must flow through a qualified domestic charitable trust or charitable institution. There is no free repatriation of the original endowment principal; liquidation proceeds are strictly controlled and need SAFE and civil affairs approval. The entire FX architecture is therefore transaction-based, product-specific, and highly fact-driven, with no umbrella convertibility entitlement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Since the 2012 reform, no mandatory conversion ratio applies to export foreign currency receipts. Exporters must repatriate the full amount of proceeds into China within 180 days after the date of receipt, unless an extension is approved by SAFE. The exporter may retain up to 100% of the foreign currency in an export settlement account with a licensed bank, or sell the proceeds to a designated bank as RMB. Each receipt must be matched to the customs declaration and the trade contract in the Cross-Border Receipt and Payment Verification System.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account for FDI registration and escrow of original capital injection

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Settlement Account (RMB) for daily grant disbursements and operating expenses
Capital Verification Holding Account and RMB Special Account for charitable fundraising
Secondary Grant Disbursement Account for domestic grant payments

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital fintech EMI providers, such as Revolut Business, Airwallex, and Payoneer, do not hold a mainland China banking licence and are legally barred from providing domestic settlement, clearing, or deposit services to PRC-incorporated entities. A WFOE must maintain its primary treasury and clearing infrastructure with a SAFE-licensed domestic commercial bank. Foreign EMIs can only provide ancillary offshore collection accounts for inbound donations before funds are wired into the WFOE's onshore capital account; they cannot serve as the primary clearing rail or hold RMB balances for the entity. Therefore, the viability of fintech EMIs is rated Low and their use is restricted to off-China currency pools.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person attendance is mandatory for the statutory legal representative, the executive director, and the compliance officer of the WFOE for initial account opening. Remote consular proxy opening is not recognised under PRC banking practice. The KYC interview must take place in the physical branch of the Tier-1 bank, with original identification documents and company chops stamped on each signature page. For foreign shareholder entities, apostilled or consular-legaised certificate of incorporation and certificate of incumbency are required, and the beneficial owner's identification must be verified by a notary before the interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between the registration purpose as a private charitable foundation and the WFOE's corporate structure as a foreign-owned limited liability company; the bank may suspect that grants are used as disguised profit extraction or money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of formation under the Charity Law, foundation bylaws with restricted grant-making clauses, statutory audit reports, beneficiary due diligence policy, and a sworn declaration that no founder, director, or beneficial owner receives any grant or loan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incoming cross-border donations from multiple small offshore donors or shell trust structures without clear source-of-funds documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth declarations from each donor, notarised donor identification and bank reference letters, a full trust deed if the donor is a trust, and a consolidated contribution registry identifying each donation above USD 50,000.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Endowment investments in equities, funds, or structured products without a license for charitable trust management may breach China's non-profit regulatory framework.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A licensed PRC charity trust agreement, investment mandate with a qualified securities or trust company, monthly portfolio statements, and an internal investment policy committee resolution approving every allocation within ISIC 6430 endowment objectives.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound payment requests to foreign grantee charities without prior SAFE surrender or approval codes could be blocked as cross-border capital flight.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Overseas grantee registration certificates, grant agreements approved by the board, OFAC and sanctions screening reports, SAFE pre-filing approval or duty-paid records, and evidence that the endowment capital was fully repatriated and settled in RMB before any outbound conversion.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection for the WFOE must flow from the direct offshore shareholder via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 to the Foreign Exchange Capital Account at a designated domestic bank. The remittance instruction must carry SAFE purpose code 622 - Foreign Investment Capital, plus the unique FDI registration code. On receipt, the bank updates the SAFE system and issues a receipt voucher. The entity then appoints a PRC licensed accounting firm to produce a capital verification report, which is filed with the Administration of Market Regulation and the bank before funds may be converted to RMB. Conversion is executed under the bank's converted settlement account, and every utilisation of the converted RMB must be checked against the negative list, under the supervision of the People's Bank of China.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade disbursements, the WFOE will use SWIFT MT103 as the standard customer credit transfer for service fees and licensing royalties, complemented by commercially issued letters of credit (MT700) and documentary collections (MT400/MT420) for physical goods. All outbound grant distributions to foreign charitable beneficiaries must be prefaced by an application for cross-border payment under the service/trade item, and the bank will require the relevant contract, invoice, approval certificate, and grant resolution. Disbursement escalation over USD 500,000 triggers enhanced review by the bank's FATF desk and may require SAFE approval.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward contracts (FX forwards) with tenor up to one year, linked to genuine trade and grant disbursement exposure, with 10-20% margin requirement

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) between RMB and USD/EUR/JPY/HKD for long-term foreign-exchange exposure on registered foreign capital and statutory dividend or royalty schedules, subject to SAFE prior approval

Currency swap boundaries: only outright swaps on actual current or capital account flows may be booked; NDFs (non-deliverable forwards) and synthetic forwards are strictly prohibited onshore for Chinese resident entities, and no net-settlement based hedging is available

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Credit Information Report (Annual Filing of the Enterprise Information Public Disclosure System)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - local Market Regulation Administration through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: From 1 January to 30 June every year for the immediately preceding fiscal year; final due date is 30 June at 23:59 local time
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing: enterprise is transferred to the Directory of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations within 10 working days; 3 consecutive years of non-filing results in inclusion in the List of Seriously Illegal and Discredited Enterprises, administrative revocation of the business license, and disqualification/credit blacklisting of the legal representative.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Annual Information Report (annual foreign investment information filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) through the integrated SAMR Enterprise Registration and Annual Reporting System, coordinated with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same annual window as the enterprise credit report: 1 January through 30 June for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or false filing: MOFCOM issues a correction order with a 20-working-day cure period; overdue correction attracts a fine of RMB 20,000 (approx. USD 2,800) to RMB 200,000 (approx. USD 28,000); deliberate misrepresentation or concealment may attract penalties up to RMB 500,000 (approx. USD 70,000), publication on the non-compliant foreign-invested enterprise directory, and cross-departmental restrictions on foreign exchange settlement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Settlement Return (enterprise income tax annual reconciliation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) - local tax bureau of the competent jurisdiction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 31 May for the preceding fiscal-year income and expenses; due by 31 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: fixed monetary penalty of RMB 2,000-10,000 (USD 280-1,400) plus daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% on the unpaid tax; understated or fraudulent income is characterised as tax evasion, subject to 50%-500% penalty on underpaid tax, possible criminal prosecution when evaded tax exceeds RMB 50,000 and exceeds statutory percentages, and adverse credit record affecting the legal representative and annual licence renewals.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Annual Financial Statements Audit and Certified Auditor's Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) for inspection and public-filing readiness; shareholders' meeting or board of directors receives the signed auditor's report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the end of the fiscal year (usually on or before 30 April) so that the audited accounts are ready for shareholder approval and the 31 May / 30 June statutory filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to have annual financial statements audited violates the Company Law; for a single-member limited WFOE the previous statutory regime imposed a fine of RMB 10,000-100,000 on the company; under the 2023 Company Law, uncertified statements are treated as unlawful, rendering the annual reports unacceptable to SAMR, disqualifying the charitable endowment licence if applicable, and triggering abnormal listing and legal-person credit sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Charity/Endowment Activity Report and Financial Declaration (for licensed charitable endowment management activity under the Charity Law)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Civil Affairs (MCA) / local Civil Affairs Bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year, i.e. by 31 March for a calendar-year endowment/foundation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-submission or false submission: administrative warning and correction order; serious violation leads to public naming, de-registration of charitable status, loss of tax-exempt status and pre-tax deduction qualifications, prohibition of fundraising and grant distribution, and, where charitable property is misused, criminal liability for the responsible directors under the Criminal Law.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: (1) General threshold: zero - every limited liability company in China, including every WFOE regardless of size, balance-sheet total, turnover or employee count, is statutorily required by the PRC Company Law to engage an independent licensed CPA firm to audit its annual financial statements. (2) Sector-specific quantified triggers applicable to a charitable endowment management entity: mandatory independent CPA audit where annual charitable/endowment receipts exceed RMB 1,000,000 (approx. USD 140,000), year-end assets exceed RMB 5,000,000 (approx. USD 700,000), or the organisation has more than 20 full-time paid staff. (3) For financial/trust-type regulated funds: audit is also compulsory where assets under management exceed RMB 100,000,000 (approx. USD 14,000,000) or the number of grant beneficiaries exceeds 50. Additional any: listed company, CSRC-regulated company with turnover > RMB 20,000,000 (approx USD 2,800,000) or total assets > RMB 50,000,000 (approx USD 7,000,000).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS, substantially converged with IFRS) for the statutory audit; smaller non-listed entities may use the Small Enterprise Accounting Standards (CAS-SME) if eligible; a charitable endowment undertakes a supplementary entity-level report under the Accounting System for Non-Governmental Non-Profit Organizations with the audited annual report prepared under CAS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the PRC Measures for the Registration and Supervision of Beneficial Owners of Corporate Entities, a WFOE must identify and report beneficial owner data to the SAMR within 30 days of any change, including any transfer of shares in the offshore or domestic equity chain; there is no stand-alone annual UBO confirmation return in China, but the annual Enterprise Credit Information Report must be used to reconfirm controlling shareholder and ultimate beneficiary information each year. Any equity transfer must be registered with SAMR within 30 days; failure to perform triggers orders to rectify, fines up to RMB 50,000 (approx. USD 7,000) on the entity and RMB 10,000 on the responsible legal representative.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - USD 1,500 per annum for a standard registered-office address and local corporate-compliance agent in tier-1/tier-2 Chinese cities; premium services in Shanghai/Beijing range from USD 2,000 to USD 3,000.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - USD 5,000 for a standard trading/services WFOE; USD 6,000 - USD 12,000 for a charitable endowment licence holder with substantial fund-flow and grant-making activity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying non-profit organizations may obtain CIT exemption for certain income derived from donations and statutory funds; High-and-New Technology Enterprises eligible for 15% rate; Small Low-Profit Enterprises taxable at 20% with possible temporary reductions; qualified technology transfer income may be exempt or taxed at half-rate; R&D expenses enjoy a 100% additional deduction (200% total deduction).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form Type A, 2017 revision as amended) submitted via the State Taxation Administration Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) online portal; quarterly prepayment returns filed through same system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly prepayment returns due within 15 days after each calendar quarter-end; annual reconciliation return due on or before May 31 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification and registration profile: legal name of WFOE, unified social credit code, registered address, date of incorporation, and PRC tax residence status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirms the entity is a PRC resident enterprise as a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) and not a non-resident enterprise; note that the place of effective management must be in mainland China to avoid PE concerns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Industry classification and business scope: ISIC 6430 / private charitable foundation and endowment management.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Embed the charitable foundation license status; any deviation into commercial activity may jeopardize non-profit income exemption and trigger standard CIT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting basis and functional currency: select Chinese accounting standards and CNY as reporting currency; foreign currency transactions translated per PBOC published rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border grant disbursements in USD must be translated at the spot rate on transaction date; undrawn foreign endowment balances must be re-measured; adjustments impact taxable profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income schedule: include operating income, investment income, donation-related income, management fees, interest, and other revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a charitable-endowment WFOE, substantiate whether each income stream is within the exempt category for qualified non-profit organizations; passive income from controlled foreign affiliates must be reported at arm's length and subject to transfer pricing adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable income and exempt income claimed: indicate exemptions such as qualified donation funds, statutory-purpose endowment income, and technology transfer income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders and foreign founders must supply legal evidence of qualified non-profit status; improper exemption claims are a red flag for shell-entity anti-abuse review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and cost allocation: general administration, charitable grant expenses, depreciation, research expenditure, salaries, and cross-border service charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All payments to non-resident affiliates (royalties, management fees, recharged services) must satisfy beneficial ownership, economic substance, and withholding tax documentary requirements; excessive allocations are adjusted by BEPS-style transfer pricing audits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income and loss carryforward computation: aggregate income less deductions, exemptions, and permitted carried losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Directors must verify that the 5-year loss carryforward limit applies; charitable foundations cannot indefinitely accumulate paper losses without actual philanthropic activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable tax rate calculation: 25% standard rate; apply reduced rates or exemptions only if statutory qualifications exist.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If treaty protection is needed for parent-company income, disclose the treaty benefits in the supplementary schedules; no rate reduction is permitted without TRC and beneficial ownership filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit offset (county/region specific) and double-taxation relief for foreign-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders repatriating profits shall treat the PRC WFOE as a resident enterprise; any foreign tax credit claimed by the WFOE must be separately documented and subject to anti-abuse verification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction disclosure and contemporaneous transfer pricing summary schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory when controlled transactions exceed the statutory thresholds; include local file, master file, and country-by-country report if consolidated group turnover surpasses RMB 5.5 billion.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or failure to file: Tax Collection Administration Law Art. 62 imposes a fine of RMB 2,000-10,000 (or RMB 10,000-50,000 in serious cases) and a daily late interest charge of 0.05% on unpaid tax for each overdue day. Failure to keep TP documentation triggers fines under Public Notice [2016] No. 42 and may result in deemed adjustment plus penalty up to 300% of the underpaid tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Non-Resident Enterprise Income Tax Withholding Return (Form WHT-?; used by the WFOE as withholding agent) submitted via the State Taxation Administration e-Tax system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Transaction-based, triggered on each payment of dividend, interest, or royalty to a non-resident enterprise.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: WITHIN 7 DAYS after the actual payment date or due date of the cross-border remittance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding agent details: WFOE name, tax registration ID, address, and contact.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE is the legal withholding agent for non-resident enterprise income tax (CIT Art. 37-38) and faces primary liability for failure to withhold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident payee details: name, jurisdiction of residence, registration number, and tax identification in foreign country.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify the payee is the beneficial owner; a tax-residency certificate (TRC) from the foreign tax authority must be obtained and retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income type classification: dividend, interest, royalty, rent, or other property gain paid by the Chinese resident WFOE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Characterization directly determines the statutory 10% withholding rate and possible treaty reduction; interest with underlying commercial debt must be distinguished from equity dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross payment amount in CNY and original currency.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the full gross amount before WHT; no deduction is permitted for the tax itself unless the contract contains a gross-up provision.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Special treaty treatment indicator and rates: state the applicable Double Tax Agreement (DTA) and the treaty article.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty relief is not automatic; the payer must file an advance treaty-benefit application under Public Notice [2019] No. 35 or self-assess the conditions prescribed by the MTA, including substantive economic presence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Beneficial ownership and substance declaration: designation of the real economic owner and controlling ownership ratio.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Flag any conduit structure with no CIGA; Chinese authorities will deny treaty rate on the grounds of beneficial ownership under Notice [2018] No. 9 and BEPS recommendations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax calculation and remittance ledger: tax at 10% or reduced treaty rate less any prior prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The amount must be remitted to the national tax treasury within 7 days; a director knowingly spreading false treaty documentation triggers criminal liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold or remit WHT: TCAL Art. 69 authorizes the tax administration to recover the unpaid tax from the withholding agent and imposes a fine of 50% to 300% of the unwithheld amount; late remittance triggers daily 0.05% surcharge and travel bans on the responsible legal representative if the debt exceeds judicial thresholds.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding tax on dividends, interest and royalties paid to non-resident enterprises (CIT Law Art. 37), reduced to 5% under certain DTAs such as China-Hong Kong DTA where the beneficial owner holds at least 25% of the paying company's shares.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Step 1: Obtain the foreign shareholder's Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the jurisdiction of residence. Step 2: Complete and file the Non-Resident Treaty Benefit Application using the e-Tax portal (or self-assess under Announcement [2019] No. 35) before payment. Step 3: Submit the WFOE's certificate of residence, audited financial statements, board resolution authorizing the dividend, and evidence of beneficial ownership (including actual headcount, premises, and decision-making functions in the foreign shareholder). Step 4: The taxing authority will review the LOB/PPT test; a nominee or shell parent with no economic substance will be denied treaty benefits. Step 5: After payment, file the withholding return and attach the approved relief certificate within the statutory 7-day window.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT for interest and royalties is 10% each. Treaty rates vary: typically 10% for interest under China-OECD DTAs; royalties for industrial, scientific, or literary property usually reduced to 10%, 7%, or 5% depending on the treaty (e.g., 5% under China-Singapore DTA, 7% under China-Hong Kong DTA). Interest derives from intercompany debt must carry full written loan or debenture agreement and arm's length documentation; royalties require registered IP ownership and actual use in the PRC service.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CNY 200 million for tangible property transactions, CNY 100 million for intangible property transfers and financial transactions, CNY 40 million for other related-party transactions; a master file is required when combined annual controlled transactions exceed CNY 1 billion (or consolidated group revenue exceeds CNY 5.5 billion for country-by-country reporting).
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China has no formal ESR regime, but the PRC GAAR (CIT Art. 47), the anti-beneficial-ownership rules in Notice [2018] No. 9, and the statutory substance-over-form principle require every cross-border arrangement to demonstrate genuine Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in the PRC. For a charitable foundation WFOE, economic substance is evidenced by regular board meetings, actual grant-making processes, charitable program staffing, local bank accounts, and public-benefit activity; a shell entity with passive foreign assets and no PRC operational substance will be ignored for tax purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold Non-Resident Tax on Cross-Border Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE declares and pays a USD 2 million dividend to a foreign shareholder in a treaty jurisdiction but does not withhold or remit the statutory 10% non-resident withholding tax, presenting an inapplicable treaty exemption without filing a TRC or proving beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CIT Law Arts. 37-39 and Tax Collection Administration Law Art. 69 allow the tax authority to collect the unpaid WHT directly from the WFOE as withholding agent and impose a fine of 50% to 300% of the unremitted amount; late payment triggers a daily 0.05% surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who order the payment ignore signed compliance obligations and are treated as directly accountable persons: they face administrative penalties, a personal tax blacklisting with travel bans, potential personal restitution of the uncollected tax, and criminal prosecution if the deliberate concealment exceeds RMB 1 million, leading to imprisonment of up to 7 years under Art. 201.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sham Charitable Foundation / Shell Non-Profit Structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE obtains charitable foundation registration under ISIC 6430 and claims non-profit CIT exemption and treaty-reduced withholding rates while engaging in no actual grant-making, holding no staff in mainland China, and managing almost all assets through foreign tax-haven custodians; the foundation is therefore an artificial shell lacking core income-generating activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The PRC General Anti-Avoidance Rule (CIT Art. 47) empowers the tax authority to disregard the foundation's legal form, recharacterize all earnings as fully taxable profits at 25%, and impose a fine of 50%-500% under TCAL Art. 63; the Ministry of Civil Affairs may revoke the foundation's registration under Charity Law and issue a RMB 20,000-200,000 fine for operating without genuine charitable purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts pierce the corporate veil because the foundation form is used as a fraud device: directors are jointly liable for misapplied endowment assets, forced to repatriate diverted charitable funds, placed on the tax and civil-society blacklist with travel and conscription bans, and in cases of major charitable asset fraud are subject to up to 10 years in prison under Criminal Law articles 224 and 266.
